run: fourth sweep of 2026-08-09, written into the free -run2 filename slot

window.note: run_state.window_end already equalled today (STEP 1B case b) for the second time in the day. Window re-covered unchanged and run_state not moved. Three run logs already existed for today and this run targeted what they recorded as unswept.

not_checked_rationale: All of these were checked by one of the three earlier runs today and the window is unchanged, so re-checking them would have re-covered ground rather than adding any.
anomalies: SECOND SAME-DAY RE-RUN OF THE DAY, FOURTH SWEEP OVERALL. run_state.window_end was already 2026-08-09. Treated as STEP 1B case (b): window_start and window_end both left at 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-09.

RUN LOG DISCOVERY HOLE, NOW CLOSED. STEP 1B says to count upward from runs/<today>.json until one 404s. runs/2026-08-09.json exists and runs/2026-08-09-run3.json exists, but runs/2026-08-09-run2.json did NOT - the third run skipped the -run2 slot. A future run following STEP 1B literally would have stopped at the -run2 404 and never seen -run3. This run therefore wrote its log into the free -run2 slot to make the chain contiguous, even though it is chronologically the fourth. The numbering no longer matches run order and a human should decide whether the filenames or the counting rule should change.

GAP-FILL OUTSIDE THE WINDOW. The USDA FAS World Agricultural Production circular carries a published_date of 2026-07-10, before window_start. It is the CURRENT circular - it states its own successor is due 2026-08-12 - and no run has ever checked this source, whose manifest last_publication was null. Eleven of this run's 22 rows come from it. Precedented by the second run's COCERAL and Cooperativas gap-fill.

SERIES COLLISION AVOIDED, SAME CLASS AS THE THIRD RUN'S. ECIU's -2.5 Mt shortfall would have joined the same GB|united kingdom|mixed_grains|production|ECIU series as a001's 19.5 Mt outturn, putting a delta and a level on one chart. p016's region is qualified to 'United Kingdom (shortfall against earlier forecasts)' so the series stay apart. This is the second run in a row to work around the absence of a level-vs-change distinction in the schema; it needs a human decision.

ONE ROW CARRIES A REVIEW_FLAG THAT IS NOT A BADGE ISSUE. p013 records World Weather Attribution's 3.5C figure via Munich Re. The quote supports the number exactly; what is weak is the step from the number to an agricultural impact. Flagged rather than dropped.
NO SERIES GAINED A SECOND READING. All 21 new series are single-reading and are kept, not pruned. series_chartable stays at 4.

ONE SERIES STILL HAS MORE THAN ONE READING AND NO LABEL, unchanged across all four runs today: GB|united kingdom|winter_wheat|condition_good_excellent|AHDB, readings 2026-06-29:64 and 2026-06-29:58. It is also blocked by the c014/c015 conflict flags, so a label alone will not chart it.

raw.githubusercontent.com WAS REACHABLE THIS RUN (HTTP 200 on every index file), contradicting the previous two run logs which recorded it as blocked by the sandbox proxy. The block appears to be intermittent rather than permanent; STEP 1 as written did work here.

SOUTHERN AFRICA SEARCH RETURNED STALE RESULTS. A pass-2 search for Southern African maize surfaced almost entirely 2025-dated material (15.8 Mt South Africa 2025, Zimbabwe 1.3 Mt 2025/26). Nothing was recorded from it; the region is instead covered from USDA FAS, which is current. Worth knowing that this query shape is unreliable for the region.

MPOB NOT CAPTURED AND THAT IS CORRECT. The July supply and demand report is due 2026-08-10, one day after this run. Analyst survey figures circulating ahead of it (1.76 Mt, +7.4%) are forecast commentary on unmapped or drop-listed hosts and fail the capture bar.

USDA FAS World Agricultural Production: next circular due 2026-08-12, stated in the July circular itself.
